text:
Nora: tiny domestic emergency 1"); ok not really. planning a mellow night: vinyl + reading by lamplight. looking for 'cottagecore' or pastoral music recs (acoustic, minimal folk, field recordings). also slow cinema recs if anyone has a 2-hour wandering film. :seedling:

Ben: YES. For vinyl vibes: Vashti Bunyan 'Just Another Diamond Day', Nick Drake 'Pink Moon', Linda Perhacs 'Parallelograms'. All short, fragile songs.

Priya: If you want ambient field recordings: Chris Watson 'El Tren Fantasma' or Andy Snaith. perfect for simmering soup in background.

Luis: slow cinema: try 'The Turin Horse' (Bela Tarr) or 'Once Upon a Time in Anatolia' (Kiarostami). very patient, beautiful shots. not much plot but great for zoning out.

Hannah: book recs: 'The Keeper of Lost Things' (cozy, slightly magical) or 'The Long Earth' if you want something a bit weirder but quiet. tea pairing: earl grey + honey.

Nora: @Ben adding those to my wishlist. any recs for modern minimal composers that feel 'outdoorsy'? not synthetic ambient.

Ben: check Sufjan's quieter stuff ('All Delighted People' ep) and Balmorhea (instrumental post-classical). Also this low-run label 'Tompkins Square' has a lot of reissues.

Priya: tiny playlist I threw together:
```
1. Vashti Bunyan - Train Song
2. Ólafur Arnalds - For Now I Am Winter (piano version)
3. Balmorhea - Remembrance
4. Field Recordings - Morning on the Farm
5. Nick Drake - Northern Sky
```
Link: (sending in thread)

OpsBot: Quick poll created: option A vinyl/acoustic, option B slow film. Results after 10m: A 4, B 2.

Luis: also if you like soundtracks that feel pastoral: 'Embrace of the Serpent' score is gorgeous. not exactly cottagecore but very natural.

Hannah: pro tip: dim lights, put a kettle on, read outside if weather permits. instant ambience. :tea:

Nora: love this. setting intention: vinyl + The Turin Horse on low volume to have visuals while I read. thanks y'all :heart:
